title: First Contact
tagline: The moment everything changes — your first packet crosses into active territory.
description: You have a complete passive intelligence picture of the Meridian Financial network. Now the engagement goes active. Before scanning a single port, professionals answer one question: which systems are actually alive? Learn host discovery from first principles — what 'alive' means on a network, how ICMP works, why firewalls make hosts appear offline when they are not, and how TCP probes reveal hosts that ping cannot.
author: Cyber Learn Team
learningObjectives: Explain why host discovery precedes port scanning — what goes wrong if you skip it
Describe what 'alive' means for a networked system from first principles: IP addresses, packets, and responses
Explain how ICMP echo request and echo reply work, and what a successful ping proves
Explain why a non-response to ping does not prove a host is offline
Describe TCP-based host discovery and when it reveals hosts that ICMP cannot
Use Nmap host discovery flags to identify live hosts in an IP range
Document host discovery results in an engagement log with method, timestamp, and professional interpretation
skills: Running Nmap host discovery with ICMP and TCP probe types
Interpreting host discovery output — including the ambiguous 'no response' case
Recognising ICMP filtering and applying TCP probes as a follow-up
Documenting live host findings professionally in an engagement log
